newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan gold imports plunge on fragile demand.
newsitem.headline: Japan gold imports plunge on fragile demand.

text.p: Japan's gold imports plunged in the first seven months of this year compared with the same period last year, pushed down by fragile demand from the investment and jewellery sectors, precious metal industry officials said on Wednesday.
The sluggish trend is expected to continue for the rest of the year, they added.

"Gold demand from the investment sector has been particularly weak as interest in gold has cooled off since earlier this year, due to the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar, which pushed up gold retail prices," a senior official of a bullion house said.
Gold imports in July were down 49.98 percent from a year earlier to 11.97 tonnes, Finance Ministry data released on Wednesday showed.

Imports have fallen on a year-on-year basis since March, the data showed, while imports for the first seven months of this year totalled 95.55 tonnes, sharply down from 178.73 tonnes in the same period last year.
On Wednesday, the retail price of gold was quoted at 1,396 yen per gram, against a 20-year low of 1,070 yen on May 29 last year.
"Unless the retail price of gold slips by 20 or 30 percent from the current levels, gold demand for the investment sector is unlikely to recover," the bullion house official said.
An official at another bullion house said he anticipated Japan's gold imports for the whole year to fall by at least 100 tonnes, against 262.30 tonnes for 1995.
He said the domestic gold jewellery production had fallen by around 15 percent so far this year from 1995.
"In addition to weak gold jewellery demand at home, continued increases in gold jewellery imports are taking away market share from local jewellery makers," he added.
